## Coal (lycanthrope)

Coal was a werewolf from Moray in the Moonshae Isles during the late 15 century DR. He was slain in the late 1470s DR.

Description
In his wolf form, Coal was a heavy brute with reddish fur and a black mark on his forehead, which was the inspiration for his name.

Relationships
He was the son of Deucala, who had been a matriarch of the Black Blood tribe in northern Moray as of the mid-to-late 15 century DR. When Deucala found the Lady Amaranth in the late 1460s DR, and raised her, the young fey woman became like a sister to Coal, and was the one who named him. Coal and his sisters were fiercely protective of Amaranth.

History
When Amaranth became the de facto leader of the lycanthropes at Caer Moray, she led them to be peaceful and productive. Only females were allowed to reside within the walls, so it became Coal's duty to travel the island and bring back news.

Following the revival of the god Malar in the late 1470s DR, the community at Caer Moray was destroyed by the Black Blood tribe in the Battle of Caer Moray, and Lady Amaranth left it behind. Coal was the only lycanthrope she asked to join her, and he helped her and her guide Lukas to follow the signs left by the goddess Chauntea that would take her to a portal in the Breasal Marsh, which in turn would take her home to Sarifal. Coal was the first to arrive at the portal, where he encountered a female wolf who seemed interested in him. Unknown to Coal, this was in fact a shapechanged druid named Eleuthra Davos, who was toying with him in order to make her lover, a swordmage known as the Savage, jealous. Unfortunately, the Savage was aware that the blood of a lycanthrope was needed to activate the portal, and he slew Coal to do so. Lady Amaranth tried to avenge him, but lost her chance when an aspect of Malar arrived, forcing her to flee through the portal.

## Coronach

A coronach was a bard lich, undead creatures who had once been magical performers who used a magic ritual to seal their soul in their instrument and grant them eternal life.

Abilities
As an undead creature, coronachs did not need to eat, drink, sleep, or breathe air. They were also resistant to turn undead and similar effects. When a coronach's body was destroyed, the spirit that animated it returned to their instrument. The instrument then faded away, only to reappear with the coronach again fully formed at the place where the coronach had first played a song as a living creature.

Coronachs were powerful spellcasters. They had access to the following spells: friends, prestidigitation, thunderclap, dissonant whispers, Tasha's hideous laughter, shield, see invisibility, silence, fear, hypnotic pattern, greater invisibility, dominate person, synaptic static, Otto's irresistible dance, forcecage, and power word, kill. They could play an overpowering dirge that would drain the life force from those nearby into the coronach. They could also use their signature instrument as a magical weapon, slamming it into foes to paralyze them.

Coronachs were also gifted with quick wits. They could use cutting words at carefully chosen moments to unbalance others. They also had the power to dramatically reveal an intimate secret of a creature within  of them, which could magically charm that target.

Society
The ritual to become a coronach involved the bard ceaselessly playing the first song they ever learned for a tenday. After this, the bard's heart would die and their soul would be stored in their instrument. Typically, to keep them nourished through the ritual, bards employed others to feed them and take care of their bodies. Once the ritual was complete, the new coronach would kill these assistants to keep their secret safe. This first song the bard ever learned was also the secret to destroying a coronach. If the coronach's instrument was ever used to play that song, both it and the bard would be destroyed in a deafening explosion. To protect themselves, coronachs kept the truth of their creations private.

Coronachs moved through the world, ceaselessly learning new stories and songs. Without this, their bodies would wither and disintegrate. Their appetite for long-forgotten tales and tunes could never be filled.

Notable Coronachs
Tagore, a tabaxi coronach and lutenist who spent time at the Growling Groghouse tavern in Undermountain in the Year of Three Ships Sailing, 1492 DR, after killing its barkeep.

## Council of Sorcerers

The Council of Sorcerers, also called the council of mages, was a faction of magic-users who nominally served the Ffolk High Kings and Queens of the Moonshae Isles and who represented the single most powerful concentration of magic power in the whole of the Isles as of the mid–14 century DR.Most early sources do not capitalize "council of sorcerers" or "council mages", suggesting the name may have been intended as an informal rather than proper name for the organization. However, later sources (such as Hall of Heroes and Villains' Lorebook) use capitalization to denote "Council of Sorcerers" as a proper name.

Activities
The Council served as advisors to the High Kings and Queens at Caer Callidyrr. Part of their role was to warn of any dark magic that might threaten the lands of the Ffolk.

During the reign of High King Reginald Carrathal in the early-to-mid 14 century DR, the Council operated with a great deal of independence to pursue their own ambitions and exert control over the lands of Callidyrr. While they ostensibly served the High King, and nominally represented a major source of strength for his military, in truth they deferred to him only as much as needed to make him believe that he was in control. Given that the Council's presence concentrated an enormous amount of magical power under the High King, they provided him with a valuable threat to keep the other Ffolk rulers obedient, however they had no interest in actually helping him subdue any rivals or unruly underlings.

With the rise of the Kendrick dynasty, the council continued to serve the High Kings and Queens.

Tactics
The Council was noted for both the patience and the fickleness of its members. They monitored current events and would intervene only occasionally to nudge the forces of society in the direction that was most suitable for them. They were widely feared and seen with suspicion by the peoples of the Moonshaes. Given the rarity of magic on the Moonshaes, the Council was regarded in almost legendary terms by some of the Ffolk, and some councilmembers were known to engage is overt shows of magical prowess to reinforce this (such as by flying over populated areas to attract attention).

Base of Operations

The Council operated out of the Palace of the High King in Caer Callidyrr. Their primary base was an eight-story circular tower atop a hill on the western side of the castle that seemed out of place amidst the rest of the grand fortress. It was only accessible via a bridge to a nearby corner tower. Many of these levels were dedicated to sleeping quarters, laboratories, and libraries, as well as to the council's meeting room at the top.

The Council would also sometimes meet in a secret cavern in the dungeon located approximately  below the castle. This high chamber featured a circular table surrounded by a dozen chairs and several pools of runoff dripping from the overhanging stalactites.

History
The council was created by the order of High King Alec Carrathal IV in the early 14 century DR (approximately thirty years before the Darkwalker War). The original council consisted of nine mages, the leader and most powerful of whom was Curmavyss, who held his leading position for about three decades. During his tenure, the council grew to thirteen members and operated with a great deal of autonomy. By the mid–14 century DR, they served the High King only in theory, and in actuality, each councilmember wielded direct control over their own small piece of Callidyrr.

In the, a Thayan mage named Cyndre arrived in the Moonshaes.Per Hall of Heroes, Cyndre arrived in the Moonshae Isles three years before the state of the region as described in Moonshae, which is understood to be set just prior to the Darkwalker War of 1345 DR. Recognizing that he was dangerous, Curmavyss sought to keep him close, and hesitantly invited him and his ally Alexei to join the Council. His concerns were well-placed, and within three years, Cyndre had arranged for Curmavyss and five of his allies on the council to be killed. Working to subvert or replace the remaining members, the Council of Sorcerers was remade in Cyndre's image as the Council of Seven.

By the, the twisted Council of Seven had allied with the likes of duergar and Hobarth, a priest of Bhaal; arranged to assassinate the kings of Snowdown, Moray, and Corwell; and worked to eradicate the druids of Alaron. Cyndre's hold over the Council was only broken when he was bound and sealed underground by the druid Robyn Kendrick at the Battle of the High Kings on Eleint 5 of that year.

The council would continue to operate in service to High King Tristan Kendrick. As of the, they worked directly for High Queen Alicia Kendrick.

Members
The council was composed of powerful mages and sorcerers who collectively wielded more arcane power than anywhere else in the Moonshaes.

In addition to the fluctuating number of mages who sat on the council, each councilmember had several students and apprentices, many of whom were considerably powerful in their own right. At its height in the mid–14 century DR, the total number of magic-users affiliated with the Council exceeded 50.

Notable Members
 Curmavyss, the original leader of the council.
 Cyndre, who usurped control of the council around the time of the Darkwalker War.
 Alexei, an ally to Cyndre who ultimately turned against him.
 Keane, an apprentice who joined in the .

## Coram the Warrior

Coram the Warrior was a human leader who founded the realm of Coramshan in the 61 century before Dalereckoning.

History
Following the entrapment of Calim and Memnon in  inside the Calimemnon Crystal, their realms fell apart while their surviving servants (mainly lesser genies) struggled to maintain their domains. Shortly after in, rebel humans slaves and servants allied with the dwarves of Shanatar, forming an army led by Coram the Warrior to fight the remaining genie overlords. His army ultimately ended the genie domination of the region by, and Coram declared himself ruler of the lands between the Calim Desert and Marching Mountains. They rebuilt Calimport and Keltar, naming this new realm Coramshan in honor of both Coram and Shanatar.

Despite his personal success, Coram's nine sons slew each other and ended their dynasty within 32 years, and the first 50 years of the realm saw over 300 rulers and heirs slain as they jockeyed for the throne.

## Corin Dryden

Novice Corin Dryden was a servant of the Silver Flame in the world of Eberron.

Description
Corin was a young man with short brown hair and large sideburns. He carried a mace and wore a surcoat of the Silver Flame with a suit of chainmail.

History
During the Darkening of Faerûn, Corin attached himself to senior Inquisitor Gnomon, hoping that he could escape his family's poor legacy with faithful and wise service to the Silver Flame. When Brother Dectaran found the hidden base of the Lords of Dust in Stormreach, Corin followed along as Gnomon burst in on an aggressive assault. Unfortunately for Corin, Gnomon was actually a rakshasa spy and led him into an ambush, letting him be beaten near to death as Gnomon attempted to outrun the Silver Flame's pursuit. It was unknown whether Corin survived the encounter or not.

## Company of the Chimera

The Company of the Chimera was a mercenary company of Sembia in the late 14 century DR.

Organization
The captain of the company was Tombli, a duergar halfblood. They numbered roughly one hundred.

Activities
While they may have taken up other tasks before, they were so disastrous at guard duty that their wardenship had once been described as worse than rampant brigandry.

Relationships
The company had allies throughout Sembia and the Dales.

History
In Marpenoth of the, the Company of the Chimera was contracted to guard a  stretch of the Dawnpost highway and a Sembian waystation by some moneyed interest from that country. By Marpenoth 21, they had spent two tendays stationed at the Inn of the Seven Silvers. That day, there was an altercation between the captain, Tombli, and one of his warriors, the Uthgardt barbarian Saskia.

By the next day, Saskia had fled the company after helping free the pseudodragon Aeristhax, which Tombli had purchased from a passing merchant; she fully believed the company would pursue her north.

## Cognizance crystal

Cognizance crystals, also known as crystal capacitors, were psionically charged arrays of rock crystals that allowed psionics users to store psionic energy for later use, acting like the psionics equivalent to a pearl of power.

Description
Resembling elaborate jewelry, they consisted of a one central crystal with two or three smaller ones arranged around it in specific positions by silver wire. These crystals gave off a faint glow so long as they were full of psionic energy as well as a faint psychokinetic psionic aura. The glow they emitted could vary in coloration, such as golden or purple. Altogether a set of cognizance crystals weighed around .

Some were known to hang cognizance crystals from belts or necklaces, whilst others were found to wrap them around the ends of rods or staves.

Abilities
A user had to attune to these crystals by holding them or having them on their person for a period of 10 minutes before they could be used. They could be used by both psionics users and psionic creatures. When activated, the wielder was able to use a crystal's stored pool of psionic energy in manifesting any psionic powers that the user knew. They could not, however, be drawn upon to replenish a wielder's own pool of mental energy.

Once depleted of its stored energy, a psionics user could restock a cognizance crystal by using a complex series of asanas, redirecting their own mental energy from the muladhara chakra into it. However, a cognizance crystal could never store more psionic energy than it was originally created to hold.

Value
The value of a cognizance crystal varied depending upon the most powerful psionic power that it could manifest with its stored pool of psionic energy. The lowest possible value of was 1,000 gp, whilst the highest was 81,000 gp.

Notable Users
 The Kaliesh'erai, a psionic elven organization, kept a number of powerful crystal capacitors within the subbasement vaults of their hall in Evereska.
 Tanju, a member of the Hlondeth militia in the 14 century DR. His cognizance crystal consisted of a trio of quartz, one clear, one rosy, and one smoky. When active they gave off a faint purple glow.
 Zelia, a powerful yuan-ti telepath, scorned crystal capacitors as being "crutches" that one could become overly reliant upon.

Trivia
 Earth nodes functioned similarly to crystal capacitors, though they had twice the storage potential and naturally regenerated any energy drawn from them on a daily basis.
 Metaminds could make their psicrystals function like a cognizance crystal.

## Cobra

Cobras were a type of venomous snake recognizable by their expandable hoods.

Description
Cobras were  long, with scales ranging from the green and brown to pinkish tan and even completely black. Their hoods were associated with the species, and most subspecies had decorative formations on their hood scales.

Subspecies
The subspecies called the Black Cormyrian cobra was found in interior Faerûn and was more used to the colder climate than other kinds of cobras.

Combat
About four in ten cobras were able to spit their venom against foes, while the rest had to use their bites to deliver their dangerous toxin. Those able to spit would do so to blind their target, as the toxin, if it entered the eyes, quickly began destroying the eye tissue, blinding them within a minute unless rinsed quickly with water or other liquid.

The true danger of cobras was from their bites, however, as the venom would begin paralyzing the unlucky recipient in a matter of seconds. Their muscles would lock up and even speech became very difficult. Within two to six minutes this was accompanied by violent vomiting, followed by death by asphyxiation.

Ecology
Usually only hunting at night, cobras would feed on small rodents, reptiles, and insects.

Habitats
Cobras were endemic to the Chultan Peninsula, and were found in Zakhara, sometimes used as guardians by those living there.

While arboreal cobras were found in the dense jungles hunting and attacking from the trees, the spitting variety were never arboreal, instead inhabiting the tall grasses of plains and light jungles where foliage was less dense.

History
Cobras were sometimes used by snake charmers to dance along to a tune. Usually these cobras would have had their fangs removed to prevent them from biting their handlers.

A coiled cobra was the symbol of the god Set of the Mulhorandi pantheon.

In the ancient Shoon Imperium, all coins from the copper cardey to the platinum nirdey bore the imperial seal of two scimitars bound together at the handles by a rearing cobra, its hood fully expanded as if ready to bite or spit.

## Coprates Bile

Coprates "Cap'n" Bile was a privateer in the Sea of Fallen Stars during the mid-to-late 14 century DR. She was briefly involved in a mission to connect Selgaunt with Myth Nantar militarily.

Description
Coprates Bile was  tall and, with brown hair and eyes. Her skin had a ruddy tan.

Personality
People agreed she was rude and obnoxious, but the onus of her efforts was in running a tight ship, not observing the manners of city folk.

Abilities
Notably uncharismatic, she had the makings of a ranger adapted to the sea, and superior heroic strength.

Possessions
Her most notable possessions were a decanter of endless water, a ring of regeneration, and a powerful, enchanted leather armor. She also carried an ointment for sunburns.

Activities
She was the captain of the Emerald Tayar.

Relationships
Her great-uncle was Petrove, a known pirate, and Coprates held a mean grudge against sahuagin ever since they killed him. She prided herself in looking after her crew, including Rondo Marsh, her ship's mage, whose grudge against wealth and power worried her she might lose him to foolish politics. She'd also hired Ilsa Merrymore, a sea elf, to dive for shipwrecks, and turned a blind eye to her constant skimming.

During the mission to contact Serôs, she considered Sturge Whitsunday to be a popinjay who better know his place and do as he was told, and she would make sure to tell him to do things that spoiled his hair and clothes. She viewed his sister Aleine Whitsunday more favorably, taking a liking to her, and pitying that she had such a pompous fool of an older brother. Finally, she viewed Nagreous Twiddle with suspicion, finding him incomprehensible, and keeping an eye to ensure he didn't modify the Emerald Tayar.

History
Born to a middle-class family in Selgaunt, Coprates was raised on her great-uncle Petrove's sea-shanties until at thirteen she became a stowaway, disguising herself for a position as cabin boy. Within three years she'd made first mate, and three years after that, she'd saved up enough money to buy the Emerald Tayar, her ship. About a year after that, her great-uncle was killed by sahuagin, giving her a lasting grudge. She hired Rondo Marsh from the docks in Selgaunt at some point after Mirtul of the, almost a year before her mission to contact Serôs.

She was hired by Sturge Whitsunday in Mirtul of  to bring him, his sister, and the gnomish inventor Nagreous Twiddle to Myth Nantar.

Rumors & Legends
She told everyone she was the kid of a pirate queen and a sea wolf, raised by sharks.

## Commander Lightfeather

Commander Lightfeather was a carrier pigeon who worked for the Sword Coast Couriers in the Rivington neighborhood of the Outer City of Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR.

Description
Commander Lightfeather was an average-looking pigeon with gray feathers and a sheen of greens and purples around the neck. He could not speak as he was just a bird; however, one could communicate with him via magical means.

History
Lightfeather was the delusional self-proclaimed military "Commander," who supervised other carrier pigeons of the Sword Coast Couriers in . The pigeon believed that there was a war going on outside the "headquarters," and the mail he and other birds were delivering was top-secret communiqués attached to them by a "tall one." Commander Lightfeather believed he supervised the "finest aerial communication regiment this side of the Chionthar." When carrier pigeons began disappearing in the city, Lightfeather believed they were casualties of war; in reality, the birds were snatched by Tara, a tressym, that made a nest on a nearby rooftop. The tressym was searching for her friend and master, Gale Dekarios of Waterdeep, who was involved in the Absolute crisis of 1492 DR.

## Colimpha

The Colimpha was a diving bell built by Nagreous Twiddle in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.

Construction
It could seat six.

History
After Nagreous Twiddle built an experimental diving bell for the Sembian navy, he built a definitive model, the Colimpha, which he named after a patriarch of his family. That model was then brought along by Sturge Whitsunday alongside Nagreous himself for a mission to discover Myth Nantar, carrying the contraption on a barge towed by the Emerald Tayar.

The diving bell may have been the subject of tampering by Aymar Athelmeyer, a disguised malenti, who wanted to prevent Sturge from improving relationships with Myth Nantar. If so, the diving bell would become a bit less of a forward-thinking invention, and a bit more of a deathtrap, but just a bit, making it impossible to lift the diving bell back from the depths and in fact causing physical damage to its crew during descent.
